parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State Newton’s second law of motion.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
A constant resultant force F acts on an object A. The variation with time t of the velocity v for the motion of A is shown in Fig. 2.1.
{{figure:figure_2_1.png}}
The mass of A is 840 g.
Calculate, for the time t = 0 to t = 4.0 s,

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
the change in momentum of A,
change in momentum = $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The force F is removed at t = 4.0 s. Object A continues at constant velocity before colliding
with an object B, as illustrated in Fig. 2.2.
{{figure:figure_2_2.png}}
Object B is initially at rest. The mass of B is 730 g.
The objects A and B join together and have a velocity of 4.7 m $s^{-1}$.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: By calculation, show that the changes in momentum of A and of B during the collision are equal and opposite.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Explain how the answers obtained in (i) support Newton’s third law.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: By reference to the speeds of A and B, explain whether the collision is elastic.
